subject: Automotive & EVs
title: EV Affordability Gap
description: A short lesson to help you apply EV Affordability Gap.

hook.text: The average new EV still costs more upfront than the average gas car. That gap matters.

buildup.text: Battery costs make up 30–40% of an EV's price. Until those drop further, sticker prices stay high.

discovery.text: Lifetime costs often favor EVs—cheaper fuel, less maintenance, fewer moving parts to break.

twist.text: But many buyers can't afford the upfront premium, even if long-term costs are lower.

climax.text: Used EVs and sub-$25,000 models from China are starting to close the affordability gap globally.

punchline.text: EVs win on cost over time, but lose at the cash register.

quiz.question: What makes up 30-40% of an EV's price?
